hpi_details: A 32-year-old female presents to the clinic with galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and headache. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
ideas: She thinks she might have an undetected early pregnancy or a severe hormonal disruption caused by stress.
concerns: She is worried that her missed periods and breast discharge mean she has become permanently infertile.
expectations: She hopes to get a definitive blood test and medicine to regulate her hormones so her menstrual cycle returns to normal.

core_concepts: Prompt recognition and structured assessment of Prolactinoma is essential for guiding targeted diagnostic workup and clinical decision-making.
A thorough clinical history, baseline risk assessment, and targeted objective testing must be synthesized rather than relying on any single symptom in isolation.

Evaluation requires repeat prolactin measurement and exclusion of pregnancy, medication effects, hypothyroidism, and renal disease before pituitary MRI; dopamine-agonist treatment follows confirmation and is guided by tumor size and symptoms.
Diagnostic workup and therapeutic decisions should adhere to established clinical guidelines while accounting for patient-specific comorbidities.
diagnostic_clues: Chief Complaint: galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and headache

Key HPI features: A 32-year-old female presents to the clinic with galactorrhea, amenorrhea, and headache. The patient states the symptoms started recently and have been gradually worsening, accompanied by generalized fatigue.
Objective/Exam findings: Focused physical exam and vital signs check. Tailored diagnostics for Prolactinoma.
common_misconceptions: Assuming that an atypical or mild presentation rules out Prolactinoma.
Relying solely on a single normal laboratory value or imaging result to prematurely exclude pathology.
Equating temporary symptomatic relief with full resolution of the underlying condition without completing standard evaluation.
Misattributing symptoms exclusively to Pregnancy without completing a comprehensive diagnostic workup.
dangerous_errors: Failing to recognize red-flag features and delaying urgent escalation or emergency intervention.
Prematurely discharging or reassuring the patient before completing appropriate diagnostic assessment.
Initiating empirical treatment without considering major patient contraindications or drug interactions.
Ignoring critical warning signs such as: Visual field changes — suggests optic chiasm compression.
management_principles: Measure prolactin and exclude pregnancy, medication effects, hypothyroidism, and renal disease; obtain pituitary MRI for persistent unexplained elevation, then use dopamine-agonist therapy when indicated
boundaries_and_exceptions: Specific drug dosages, monitoring protocols, and referral criteria must be tailored to organ function, comorbidities, and local hospital pathways.
Atypical presentations in elderly, pediatric, or immunocompromised patients may require lower thresholds for inpatient monitoring and specialist consultation.

learning_objectives: Recognize clinical presentation and diagnostic markers of Prolactinoma
Select appropriate diagnostic workup for Prolactinoma
Implement evidence-based management plan: Confirm persistent hyperprolactinemia and exclude secondary causes before MRI and dopamine-agonist therapy

teaching.one_liner: A prolactin-secreting pituitary tumor causing inappropriate milk production, absent periods, and headache — confirmed by elevated prolactin and pituitary MRI.
red_flags: Visual field changes — suggests optic chiasm compression

must_ask.say: Are you producing milk from your breasts even though you're not breastfeeding?
Is there any chance you could be pregnant?

history.answer: My periods completely stopped about four months ago, and over the past few weeks, a milky fluid has started leaking from both of my breasts.
My periods used to be very regular, arriving every twenty-eight days and lasting about five days each time.
It has been four full months since my last menstrual bleed; they stopped all of a sudden.
Back when I was having periods, the bleeding was normal—about three to four pads a day with no large clots.
No, I haven't noticed any bleeding between my cycles or any spotting after having sex.
It's a thin, milky white liquid that comes out of both nipples, especially when my bra rubs against them or if I press on them.
I've had a dull, persistent ache in the front of my forehead for about two months, and it has been gradually getting worse.
No, my vision seems normal; I haven't had any blind spots on the sides, blurriness, or double vision.
Yes, I have been feeling unusually wiped out and exhausted over the past couple of months, even when I get plenty of sleep.
No, I haven't had any dizziness, shortness of breath, or racing heartbeats.
No, I don't have any lower belly cramps, pelvic pressure, or burning when I urinate.
No, my skin is clear without any sudden acne, and I haven't noticed any coarse dark hair growing on my face, chest, or belly.
No, I don't feel unusually sensitive to cold or heat, and I haven't noticed my throat feeling full or swollen.
My weight has been completely steady, and I haven't been on any crash diets or doing strenuous exercise.
Work is steady, and while life can be busy, I haven't experienced any overwhelming stress recently.
No, I don't get frequent nosebleeds, bleeding gums, or easy bruising, and I've never bled excessively after dental procedures.
I took a home urine pregnancy test last month and repeated another one last week, and both were negative.
I am sexually active only with my husband, and we rely on condoms consistently for birth control.
I have never been pregnant. We were hoping to start trying for a baby soon, so missing my period makes me quite anxious.
My last Pap smear was about a year ago and everything was normal, and I don't have diabetes or high blood sugar.
I'm not taking any prescription pills, birth control, stomach medications, or antidepressants; I only take a daily multivitamin.
I don't have any chronic illnesses like high blood pressure, thyroid disease, or kidney problems.
I have never undergone any surgeries and have never been admitted to a hospital.
I don't have any known allergies to medications, foods, or latex.
I have never smoked cigarettes or used electronic cigarettes in my life.
I drink occasionally, maybe one or two glasses of wine on a weekend dinner with friends.
I work as an accountant in an office and live comfortably in an apartment with my husband.
No one in my family has had pituitary tumors, hormone imbalances, or reproductive cancers.
I honestly thought I might be pregnant despite the negative home tests, or that extreme stress messed up my hormones.

I'm terrified that this means I'll never be able to get pregnant and have children with my partner. I hope you can do a definitive blood test and give me something to regulate my hormones so my cycle gets back on track.

exam.finding: Blood pressure 118/76 mmHg, pulse 72 beats/min, respiratory rate 14 breaths/min, body temperature 36.6°C, and oxygen saturation 99% on room air.
Conjunctivae are pink without pallor, and sclerae are white and non-icteric.
Pupils are equal, round, and reactive to light, and visual fields are fully intact to confrontation with no bitemporal hemianopsia.
Cranial nerves II through XII are intact, including full extraocular movements without nystagmus or diplopia.
Thyroid gland is normal in size, smooth, and non-tender, with no palpable nodules or bruit.
Bilateral breasts are symmetric with no palpable masses or skin changes; gentle manual expression yields bilateral milky white nipple discharge.
Abdomen is flat, soft, and non-tender throughout, with no palpable pelvic mass or enlarged uterus.
No acne on face or back, no hirsutism along the chin or midline abdomen, and no acanthosis nigricans on the neck or axillae.
External genitalia appear normal, vaginal mucosa is moist and pink, cervix is closed with no bleeding, and bimanual exam reveals a normal-sized, non-tender uterus without adnexal fullness.
